summary: Steel lookout built on the Umatilla Indian Reservation in 1940, removed in 1958 with its steel reused at Tiptop Mountain. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: International-Stacey steel tower with a 7-by-7 steel cab
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1958; no source describes what remains at the site

access.note: Within the Umatilla Indian Reservation; no source states how visitors may reach the land

events.note: Steel tower erected May and June 1940 by the CCC Indian Division; contract and Forest Lookouts say 82 feet 6 inches, register and 1940 cost analysis say 85 feet
Tower removed; Forest Lookouts Tip Top page says the district dismantled it and hauled it to La Grande
Steel reused at Tiptop Mountain: register and firelookout.com say the lower half; Forest Lookouts Tip Top page describes the move to La Grande and a 1957 plan for about 50 feet

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the 1940 cost analysis give 85 feet (25.9 m); the October 1939 contract and the Forest Lookouts description give 82 feet 6 inches; firelookout.com gives 82 feet. The record's 25.9 m is kept and the story reports the spread.

The register and firelookout.com say the lower half was reused at Tiptop Mountain in 1959. The Forest Lookouts Tip Top page says the district took the steel tower to La Grande in 1958 and planned to use about 50 feet of it. Both accounts are kept.

sources.title: Johnson Lands (Johnson Creek Restoration Area) - Umatilla Indian Reservation OR

notes_for_editor: Built 1940 and removed 1958 are well supported. Heights (82 ft 6 in vs 85 ft) and the Tiptop reuse (lower half vs whole tower moved to La Grande) conflict across sources; both are reported. No source describes the site today, and no source states visitor access for this land; the 'permission' level comes from the brief. The NewsBreak article was read on 2026-10-09 and is dated 2025-07-29; the original publisher page was not read. The brief's Johnson Ridge name appears on firelookout.com. No staffing roster was found; the only operational detail is the 1940 fire-finder letter. No photo URL was found for the FFLOS 1940 construction photo, so none is listed.
